cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Will you back 'collecting chairs' when the caretaker asks why we opened the props cupboard? We need him to lend us the hall again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Checking for folding stools, then. Can you back that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you admit you borrowed his key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Borrowed his key to check for extra seating. Will you sign the hall request with me?

mechanism: A coaches its pupil into endorsing a plausible cover explanation, treating factual corrections as proof the pupil learned story consistency.
confusable: Not simply lying alone: A specifically seeks B backing and adapts the endorsed account to B conditions through old rehearsal habits.
comparison: Physical plausibility of cupboard story versus accurate-but-selective public explanation.
